title: Thoughts: Mind Running / Scrolling Media and the Mind
body:
I would like to try to make and explain a comparison today. This comparison is between the modern concept of “scrolling” (almost mindlessly engaging the internet and its media) and the minds state of “running” (when we lose control of our thoughts and they appear to become randomized/uncontrollable)

While the concept of “scrolling appears to be a modern phenomenon, I would posit that it only appears such because it is a variant of an ancient human behaviour that is mostly not observable. That ancient human behaviour is the experience we call “running” thoughts.

I find myself scrolling through media particularly frequently when there is a issue in my life that either cannot be resolved by my efforts or that I do not feel emotionally/mentally prepared to face. I also find myself “scrolling” when there is nothing better for me to do with my time, which at face value appears to be a rather innocuous event. On closer inspection, and in my belief, the value statement “I have nothing better to do with my time” is dangerous, hopeless, and rather nihilistic in its nature.

The concept of a mind “running” can be outlined in several easy examples. You are lying in bed and sleep refuses to come to you. You are anxious about something and a stream of thoughts, unbidden, “sprints” through your head. You are attempting to center yourself with meditation, and your focus is continually disturbed by the stream of consciousness experience. You hear someone state you name, then state it again after a pause, and you snap out of this stream of running thoughts and realize you’ve been stopped in a grocery aisle for 15 seconds looking past the boxes of oatmeal you were shopping for. The opposing state is, you take a deep breath of fall air and twirl a leaf as your senses fill your mind with smells, temperatures, visuals, and appreciation/remorse/absurdity.

So to outline the similarities between these two events I would say that the “user” (of mind or of internet) is accessing a large pool of media within which their intentional present consciousness is subsumed. That is quite a large similarity, when the only difference is the origins of the media pool.

The difference of media pool may seem enormous. The fact the one grouping of information is personally yours and the other belongs to the incomprehensible giant that is “the internet” may try to break this comparison, but in my mind it does not. The internets pool of media is a collection of humanities thoughts rendered as writing, pictures, video, etc. Your pool of media is the same thing, except you are the only collector. But neither of them are a curator. Neither of them have a great track record of “curating” their media, their art, for you pleasure, wellbeing, or progress.

I posit that the modern phenomenon of “scrolling” is a behavioural clone of our ancient behaviour of engaging the mind “running” state. I would then also claim that both behaviours are tied to the most incredibly powerful tools this world has ever seen, and that these two behaviours represent a state of dysfunction in both arenas. Thirdly I would posit that applying personal wellness and mindfulness strategies to both tools will slowly increase the functional room we have for healthy intentional behaviour inside of each system.

The real purpose of this is to help me in understanding the consumptive nature of the internet, its relationship to our personal minds, and create some guidelines for achieving a healthy relationship with the “mind” of humanity. Our mind and its past/present/future capabilities are what have enabled us to achieve so much greatness and enact so much tragedy. So the internet too is a seething breeding ground for both the powerfully positive and the powerfully negative.

We must choose to think with intention if we are ever to have the time and space in our lives to achieve our goals. We also must SEEK with intention the information, collaboration, media, community we need on the internet if it will ever be the powerful tool it is capable of being. Please remember to observe yourself and your behaviours every day to make small changes that align you with your inner self. Remember this is not a war, but it is a difficult struggle. We are a habitual species, and redesigning habits is a long term process. Small consistent decisions make immense changes the further out you pan the zoom lense.

https://www.iste.org/explore/digital-citizenship/3-tips-balanced-digital-wellness

https://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/consumer-health/in-depth/mindfulness-exercises/art-20046356

If you have the time, read both of these pages and try to take a step today to manage your mindfulness and your digital mindfulness, and recognize that these actions give the real you space to exist in and around the automatic you. These things are vital for peace, wellbeing, and achievement. Love you all, thanks for reading, have a wonderful day.

title: Truth and Individuality
body: Improvement of one’s self should be each person’s utmost goal. In this strive to better ones self our internal selves achieve a true vision of what and who we are. And only in the truest most unfettered search for our personal bettering can we come to terms with our personal compass of our own personal reality. And what a social, cultural, or worldly view or belief on what a person’s search for bettering consists of, it shouldn’t matter, for if it is truly the most important aspect of a person’s self, it won’t matter. When we search for our true goals we move away from an outward balance based on opinions of others, and we achieve an inward balance based on our personal view of life and our surroundings. Once this has been achieved to an extent we can come to terms with the world outside, and its infinite realities based in the awarenesses around us. And through it all the ultimate truth is extracted from the monotonous and repetitive cycle of assumptions that because we are just mirrors of our genetic and physical memory, we have no self. This false assumption leads to the deprecation of one’s self, and into the spiral of despair that is found in those who have lost hope. The fact that we have that base awareness gives us an anchor on which to found our true selves.

title: Reality
body: What is our truth but experience. a young child will tell thier mother that the world is good but the mother will silently disagree. No one has lied, but two persons live in alternate realities. What is this world but a mold for the mind. a playground for our imagination. Have you ever delved so deep as to look at a plane and realize that beneath that machine are a hundred people with lives and thoughts. So complex is the idea that every thought you think is matched by millions. are we truly not the same? We all fall into the flow of life, never breaking away. What are we but failures to our own hand. Crippled by our own thoughts. Falling to the flow of our sick subjective faiths.

title: Faith, I believe
body: Faith. Faith is something no one can say is not a reality to the individual. Faith is the believing in anything. I have faith that this world could be nothing in seconds, or already is. I have faith that i know nothing. I have faith that faith is my personal subjective reality. Faiths make up our realties in their entirety. Faith is our truth. The point is, faith is law, above any other. Man law is not a true law. What is wrong and right in someone’s mind is faith, and whether it be god, karma, or compassion, that is the base of that faith, it is the only true law.

title: Self Image
body: Never let yourself be fooled, and assume that you see yourself as you would see yourself if you were someone else. Your self image is far more complex, and can only be realized when you first realize that.
